mechanism_narrative: The current level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is always associated with positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of the specific rate value.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in more than 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS is at any level.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 7.0%, it signals a weak labor market that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in more than 40% of instances when UNRATE > 7.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of below-average housing starts (HOUST < 850 thousand units) and above-average retail sales (RSAFS > 400000 million dollars) indicates a resilient consumer sector that supports equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in more than 40% of instances when HOUST < 850 and RSAFS > 400000.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (defined by rising FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above 2.5% for two consecutive months), the S&P 500 produces negative forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to increased discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in more than 40% of instances during the monetary tightening cycle.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0, it signals a contraction in the manufacturing sector that reduces corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in more than 40% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0.
